chapter_theme: Kuruntokai 261 to 280: short akam poems that weigh one day of love against a lifetime (271, 280) and the world's wealth against death (267), set the veri rite's slander against a blameless love (263), and show the returning man in the rain (270) and the friend listening for his chariot bell (275).

261.reading: The woman tells her friend that at the end of the light rains, when the old downpour has rotted the sesame pods, even in the fearful midnight when the red-eyed buffalo, weary of standing in mud, lows, her eyes do not sleep, because her heart is wounded with a grief that keeps count like the watchmen.
261.nuance: The buffalo is a field beast lowing in a hill poem's night; it does not stand for anyone, it only makes the hour audible. Lines 6 and 7 (காவலர் கணக்காய் வகையின்) seem to say she keeps the night's count as the watchmen do, so the town's guards and the lover's wakefulness are set side by side.

thinai_evidence.note: the sleepless midnight of a secret love

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative வாழி தோழி names the friend

262.reading: The friend says: let the town's gossip rise and the street clamour, and let the mother, who rails without justice, keep to her own house; the girl, her sharp teeth gleaming from the gooseberry she ate, has chosen to drink with him, in a far country on the slopes of a cross-lying hill that rises to touch the sky, the water left standing in a great tusker's footprint, like a bed dug for planting sugarcane.
262.nuance: The gooseberry is the point: its sourness makes any water taste sweet, so the girl has already prepared her mouth for the worst water of the road. The friend sets the town's noise and the mother's anger against a choice already made.

thinai_evidence.note: the girl leaves home with her lover for a far land

comparisons.tenor: the water-filled footprint of the tusker

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

263.reading: The friend says it is painful that, while the mother cuts the throat of a kid, scatters millet and, to the noise of many instruments at the forked path, praises many strange great gods who are only show and no cure for this sickness, the girl should be called possessed by a demon, when they have done no wrong to the lord of the high hill where clouds play.
263.nuance: The friend's complaint is double: the gods praised are 'other' gods (வேற்று), not the cause, and the rite's verdict, that she is possessed, is a slander on a love she calls blameless (பிழையேம்).

thinai_evidence.note: the hill and its lord; the rite of the hill country

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative தோழி names the addressee

264.reading: The woman says that the friendship the lord of the land, where on the high bank of the forest river gathered with roaring rain the dancing peacock walks with its long rustling plumes at rest and calls, formed with her out of desire, even when it bore fruit, brought her nothing she can bear.
264.nuance: The last line plays on பய: பயந்தக் காலும் (even when it yielded) against பயப்பு (yield, or the pallor of longing), so the bond's very fruit may be her pallor. The peacock only calls and walks; it carries the mood of the wet bank, not a sense of its own.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill river, the peacock and the hill lord

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

265.reading: The friend tells the girl that the lord of the rock hill, where the plump kaanthal bud, its guard of no use, opens its mouth when the bee comes, as men who know their duty open to the worthy they have long known, and its petals loosen and come free, is of good heart: when she told him the girl's state he was ashamed that it should go on so.
265.nuance: The simile is reversed: the flower is the tenor and human courtesy the vehicle, and then the whole picture is turned onto the man, whose shame works the way the bud opens, unforced, once the right one comes.

thinai_evidence.note: the kaanthal of the rock hill

comparisons.tenor: the kaanthal bud opening to the bee

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative தோழி names the addressee

266.reading: The woman wonders whether those who could cling to her broad shoulders and then leave, though they told her nothing, have also forgotten the vengai in the garden that was their sweet companion through painful nights, and the message the birds' cries carry.
266.nuance: She cannot accuse him outright, so she asks whether he has forgotten a tree: the vengai that sheltered their meetings is made a witness that he owes something to.

thinai_evidence.note: he has left her

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

267.reading: The man says that even if all the great wealth of the wide world came together at once, those who know the lawless crookedness of Death, which takes in its due order every day, would not leave the young woman with small bangles, whose white teeth hold sweet faultless water like the taste of a joint of sugarcane cut at the node, to go after work.
267.nuance: The argument from death, usually a reason to hurry after merit or wealth, is turned into a reason to stay: if life ends on Death's schedule, the hours with her are the only gain. The poet's name, காலெறி கடிகையார், is taken from line 3.

thinai_evidence.note: leaving for wealth, refused

comparisons.tenor: the sweet water of her teeth

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

268.reading: The friend says: we can neither say 'will you go?' nor ask 'will you come?'; what shall we do, friend, with him who, not minding that it was midnight, came with the thunder that splits the hooded heads of snakes and reached her long soft shoulders?
268.nuance: Both courteous questions are closed to them: asking him to go is unkind, asking whether he will come again is shameless, so the friend's helplessness is a lesson in what the secret stage forbids saying.

thinai_evidence.note: the midnight tryst in a storm

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative தோழி names the addressee

269.reading: The woman says it would be good to find someone who would go the long way without tiring and ask him, and this would be the message: father, his wound from the strong shark healed, has gone out on the blue sea, mother has gone to the salt fields to trade salt for white paddy, so if he comes now to the lord of the cold wide shore she is easy to meet.
269.nuance: The message is built out of the household's working day: the father's healed wound and the barter of salt for paddy are why the house is empty, so the fisher family's labour becomes the girl's opportunity.

thinai_evidence.note: the sea, the salt pans and the shore lord

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

270.reading: The man tells the great sky to pour now and live long, flashing to cut the deep darkness, scattering cool sweet drops and roaring, thunder on thunder, like a drum beaten hard: with the full heart of one whose work is done he has joined her and lies on the soft pillow of her fragrant hair that smells of fresh short-stemmed blue lilies.
270.nuance: The rain that in the waiting poems is the man's broken promise is here blessed: the same storm, once he is home, becomes a canopy for the union.

thinai_evidence.note: the return after the task, in the rains

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the man addresses the sky (பெருவான்)

271.reading: The woman says that trusting the lord of the land, where the clouds scatter rain like waterfalls and the rivers run full, what happened was a single day, but it has become a disease that for very many days confuses her shoulders and seizes their beauty.
271.nuance: The arithmetic carries the poem: ஒருநாள் against தவப்பன்னாள், one day of union against very many days of wasting.

thinai_evidence.note: waterfall country and the hill lord; nothing in the poem is of the fields

comparisons.tenor: the heavy rain the clouds scatter

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

272.reading: The man asks whether it will even be possible to touch the shoulders of the hill girl with dark fragrant hair, whose kohl-lined eyes are like the red-shafted arrow her brothers, when the sad young doe parted from its herd came in sight in the wide forest where whistling bowmen raised their din, drove with the bow's full force into the stag's side and drew out with its blood.
272.nuance: The arrow that is her eye belongs to her brothers, so the look that wounds him is also a weapon of her kin. Read as a hidden comparison (the stag shot near the stray doe as the suitor, the brothers as her guardians) it would be a near miss: the eye is the stated tenor, and the second pair is not anchored, so it is not tagged ullurai.

thinai_evidence.note: the hunt of the hill country and the hill girl

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

273.reading: The friend tells the bright-browed girl, cool and fragrant as the gentle evening wind that stirs the great forest so that pollen and buds tremble, that if she is hurt she will tell what she has seen: this world has been fooled like the simpleton who climbed the old cliff of the great honeycomb without a ladder; while we are here he will not leave, be sure of it.
273.nuance: The friend laughs the rumour down: those who said he would go are like a man who climbs for honey with no way to reach it. முதுமால் பறியாது is hard to construe.

thinai_evidence.note: the feared departure that will not happen

comparisons.vehicle: பெருந்தேன் கண்படு வரையின் முதுமால் பறியா தேறிய மடவோன்
comparisons.tenor: the world that expected him to leave

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative ஒண்ணுதலோயே names the addressee

274.reading: The man says that even the cruel forest, where the ukaay with thin stems like a dove's back drops its dense fruit like coins, where hard-eyed men climb its branches with bow and arrow to watch for travellers, and where the parched chew the fruit to ease their thirst, will be sweet if he goes holding the jewelled bosom of the girl whose girdle is set with gold and gems.
274.nuance: Line 8 decides whether he means to take her with him: our text and tamilvu read 'embracing' (முயகினம் / முயங்கினம்), sangamtamil.com 'thinking of' (உள்கினம்), which would make it a lone journey sweetened by memory.

thinai_evidence.note: the harsh forest road

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

275.reading: The friend says: let us climb the high rock overgrown with mullai and look, friend; is that the bell of a good grass-fed cow of the bull herd coming home to town at dusk, or are those the bells of the chariot of the man who, with the full heart of one whose work is done, comes down the wet-sand forest stream with young bowmen guarding his side?
275.nuance: The two bells, the cow's and the chariot's, are the same sound at the same hour; the friend's question keeps hope and doubt together.

thinai_evidence.note: mullai on the rock and the returning herds at dusk

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative தோழி names the addressee

276.reading: The man says that the guards who watch the bright thoyyil painted on the rising breasts of the slim-shouldered girl, as she makes dolls and wanders round the reed pond, do not even know; if he were to take his case to the just king's court of the red sceptre what would become of her? She is truly very simple, and this clamouring town is to be pitied.
276.nuance: He imagines suing a child at law: the king's court of justice is the only authority he can think of for a harm that has no culprit, and he drops the idea at once because she does not know what she has done.

thinai_evidence.note: a secret love the guards do not see

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

277.reading: The friend blesses the mendicant who eats his fill of red rice and white butter begged at a single house, at a wide doorway with no dog in a clean street, that he may get hot water in a vessel in the cold season; he asks when the north wind of the last rains will come, the wind at which she of the lightning-slim waist trembles, and the friend answers that when it comes their beloved will come.
277.nuance: The blessing is precise: a man who lives on alms in the cold season would want hot water most. Whether என்றி means 'you ask' or 'you said' decides whether the mendicant brought the promise or only the question.

thinai_evidence.note: waiting for the promised season

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: a mendicant who begs at one house (ஓரிற் பிச்சை), addressed as நீயே

278.reading: The woman says they think neither of her small soft feet, like the tender shoots of the lovely mango stirred by a strong wind, nor of the small green doll; cruel are they, friend, who crossed the mountain where the male monkey shakes down the sweet ripe fruit and the mother monkey with her young sits below and eats all she can catch.
278.nuance: The small green doll (சிறுபசும் பாவை) is the girl's plaything, but read with the monkey's young it may also be a child, which would make this a wife's poem.

thinai_evidence.note: he crossed the mountain and does not think of her

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the vocative வாழி தோழி names the friend

iraicchi.act: the male monkey shakes down ripe fruit for the mother monkey and her young, who eat it below
iraicchi.sense: even the monkey on the mountain he crossed provides for its mate and young, while he who passed it does not think of her

279.reading: The woman asks whether, even at this hour, when the clear bell tied to the striped neck of the dark ram with twisted horns rings at every step in the lonely night, he will not come, he who went past many great hills where a huge boulder the rain has forgotten to wash shines like an elephant covered in dust, and did not think of her well-jointed shoulders.
279.nuance: Two places at one hour: her village, where the flock's bell keeps ringing at night, and his road, where the rain has failed; the season she was promised has come at home but not on the hills he crossed.

thinai_evidence.note: waiting into the night of the promised time

comparisons.tenor: the dry boulder on his road

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the poem names no addressee and the colophon gives only the speaker

280.reading: The man tells his companions, long may they live, that if he could join for one day with the young woman of broad shoulders, small soft body and fine thin tresses who binds his heart every day, he would not want even half a day of life after.

thinai_evidence.note: the man's longing for union in the secret stage

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivan
thurai_akam.note: addressed to his companions (கேளிர்), who are taken to rebuke him

links.note: In Akananuru 292 the girl dreads the stranger velan's rite and the kid's killing because she would be ashamed; in Kuruntokai 263 the friend protests that the same rite praises strange gods that cure nothing and brands the girl as possessed.
links.teaches: Held together, the two poems show the veri rite wounding the secret love from both sides: to the girl it threatens exposure, and to the friend it threatens a false name, possession, for a love she insists is blameless.

links.note: Kural 804: the wise welcome the unasked acts of old friends; Kuruntokai 265 likens the kaanthal bud opening to the bee to duty-knowing men opening to the worthy they have long known, then shows the man ashamed and ready to act once told.
links.teaches: The Kural's ethic of intimacy is used in the poem as a simile for nature and then as a forecast of the lover's conduct, so the old-friendship rule becomes the friend's evidence that he will marry without being pressed.

links.note: Kural 335 says that, because death stops the tongue unannounced, good deeds must be rushed to; the man of Kuruntokai 267 argues from Death's crooked, daily taking that those who know it do not leave their women to go after work and wealth.
links.teaches: The same awareness of death leads to opposite conduct: the Kural spends the short life on merit done in haste, the lover on staying with her and refusing the journey, so impermanence by itself does not decide between duty and love.

links.note: Kural 1268: let the king fight and win, and let me join my wife and feast the evening; Kuruntokai 270: his work done, the man lies on her hair and bids the rain pour.
links.teaches: The couplet's wish is the poem's fulfilled state: the evening feast he pictured while the king's work held him is given its weather and its pillow, and the rain he dreaded on campaign becomes a blessing once he is home.

links.note: Both poems use the same line, செய்வினை முடித்த செம்மல் உள்ளம், for the man whose task is done: in 270 he says it of himself, already with her in the rain; in 275 the friend imagines it of him as she listens for a bell at dusk.
links.teaches: The formula is the hinge of the mullai return seen from both sides of the door: the friend's hopeful projection in 275 is exactly what the man claims in 270, so the waiting and the arrival are framed by one satisfied heart.

links.note: In 280 the man would give up even half a day of life after a single day's union; in 271 the woman says one day's union has become a disease lasting very many days.
links.teaches: The same single day of union is priced in opposite currencies: the man offers the rest of his life for it, and the woman, who has had it, pays in many days of wasting, so the two speakers measure the secret love by different costs.

links.note: Kural 1269: for those who wait for the day of return, one day passes like seven; Kuruntokai 271: one day of union has turned into very many days of sickness.
links.teaches: The couplet stretches the waiting days, the poem multiplies the one day of joy into a long illness, so the woman's suffering is measured not only by slow time but by a debt that a single meeting keeps collecting.

links.note: Kural 1085 asks whether her look is Death, an eye or a doe; Kuruntokai 272 likens her eyes to the bloody arrow her brothers drew from a stag near a doe parted from its herd.
links.teaches: The poem stages the couplet's three-way question as one hunt: doe, killing shaft and eye stand together, and because the shaft belongs to her brothers, the deadliness of her look is also the threat of her kin to the suitor.

links.note: In 262 the friend says the girl has chosen to drink elephant-footprint water with him in a far country; in 274 the man says the cruel forest will be sweet if he goes holding her.
links.teaches: The claim that the beloved's company sweetens the desert is made for the girl by the friend and by the man for himself, so the elopement rests on a premise both lovers hold, voiced by different speakers.

links.note: Kural 541 defines justice as investigating without favour and acting after judgement toward everyone; in Kuruntokai 276 the lover thinks of taking his case to the just king's court and at once asks what would become of her.
links.teaches: The lover's question shows where the Kural's impartial justice stops: a harm done without intent by an innocent girl is real but cannot be judged, so the just court is imagined only to be abandoned.

links.note: Kural 1124: she is to him as life when present and as death when she goes; Kuruntokai 280: for one day's union he would not want half a day of life after.
links.teaches: The couplet equates her presence with life, the poem goes further and trades the rest of life for one day of her, so the man's praise of love moves from equation to sacrifice.

source_issues: kuruntokai:269 lines 7 and 8, 270 lines 3 and 4, and 276 line 4 are repaired readings (tamilvu.org, or a TSCII leftover fixed); 273 line 8 likewise. Marked as printed.
kuruntokai:274 line 8: our text reads முயகினஞ், tamilvu.org முயங்கினம், sangamtamil.com உள்கினம்; the last would make the journey a lone one. Marked with the embrace reading and uncertain.
kuruntokai:271: the colophon says மருதம், but the poem has only hill things (அருவி, நாடன்); inferred kurinji.
kuruntokai:277: the colophon says பாலை, but the poem waits for the promised season (கடைப்பெயல் வாடை); inferred mullai.

kuruntokai:261-280: the colophons give only the speaker (… கூற்று), so thurai_akam addressees are taken from vocatives in the poems where present and given as pira otherwise, and occasion.words is null.
